abstract:
Allergic rhinitis (AR) represents a highly prevalent inflammatory disorder of the nasal mucosa, but molecular indicators capable of capturing its disease-specific transcriptional features remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to identify cell adhesion-related diagnostic biomarkers for AR and to investigate their immune relevance and molecular heterogeneity.
Publicly available AR microarray datasets were analyzed, with GSE75011 serving as the discovery dataset and GSE46171 and GSE40037 used to test the reproducibility of the diagnostic model. A predefined adhesion-related gene set was curated from MSigDB to provide the biological search space for biomarker screening. Genes showing disease-associated expression changes were overlapped with this adhesion gene set to obtain AR-associated adhesion genes. Their biological functions and interaction structure were examined through enrichment analysis, protein interaction mapping, and module extraction. Diagnostic candidates were prioritized by integrating three complementary feature-selection strategies: least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, random forest modeling, and support vector machine-recursive feature elimination. The selected markers were then assessed for diagnostic discrimination, individualized prediction, calibration performance, and potential clinical net benefit. In addition, immune infiltration, upstream regulatory networks, candidate compounds, and non-negative matrix factorization-based molecular subtypes were explored.
A total of 38 differentially expressed adhesion-related genes were identified in AR, and 13 hub genes were extracted from the key protein-protein interaction module. Integrated machine learning ultimately prioritized TNFSF14 and CD83 as diagnostic biomarkers. The combined TNFSF14/CD83 model showed strong diagnostic separation in GSE75011, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.968, and maintained external performance in GSE46171 and GSE40037, with AUC values of 1.000 and 0.758, respectively. Both biomarkers were linked to altered immune-cell features, particularly T-cell-related signatures. Using the two-marker expression pattern, AR samples could be separated into two exploratory molecular patterns that showed differences in immune profiles and enriched biological processes.
TNFSF14 and CD83 may represent promising candidate diagnostic biomarkers associated with AR-related immune alterations. These findings also reveal immune heterogeneity within AR and provide a bioinformatics-based framework for biomarker discovery and molecular stratification.
